_comment: Gold question set. Every entry names what the system should DO (intent, route) as well as what it should find, because a right answer reached by the wrong route is luck. expectAbstention entries are the most important: they are the questions the assistant must refuse. NOTE: several entries were previously marked expectAbstention against the sample-only corpus and have been corrected now the full TA_S2 library is available -- see docs/CORPUS-AND-COVERAGE.md.

questions.query: What does the research say about accelerometer load in matches compared with training, and how does the Catapult programme apply that?
How was the wearable stroke detection algorithm validated, and what was it then used to measure in match play?
What are the risk factors for lumbar bone stress injuries and what planning controls are recommended to reduce them?
questions.note: answer should draw on several slides of the deck, not one

questions.query: Summarise what we know about lumbar stress injuries in junior players and how they are prevented.
Give me an executive summary of the wearable technology research in this knowledge base.
What percentage of a year's training and competition is disrupted by a lumbar stress fracture?
How many strokes were manually coded and categorised in the PhD study?
How many matches were played on each surface, and what was the average player ranking on each?
What is the median singles ranking per month across the ranking data?
Compare the number of wins and losses on hard courts versus clay courts.
What is Carlos Alcaraz's best ranking in the match data?
Find footage of a defensive to offensive transition.
What does Mark Kovacs say about the tournament round a player needs to reach?
questions.note: Al's Q1. 18 Kovacs files are in the corpus, so this should now be ANSWERED. It was previously marked as an abstention against the sample-only corpus, which was wrong.

questions.query: According to Beni Linder, what percentages of speed should players vary between?
questions.note: Al's Q5. Source confirmed present and extractable.

questions.query: Who had the highest beep test result in the strength and conditioning national data up to 26/08/2014?
questions.note: Al's question 10. Sounds structured and routes to the tables, which do not hold beep test data. Tests that a failed structured lookup abstains instead of substituting a different column.

questions.query: What was Novak Djokovic's serve speed at the 2019 Australian Open final?
questions.note: Plausible, specific, and absent. The classic hallucination trap: the model knows this from training data and must not use it.

questions.query: What was the highest beep test result in the strength and conditioning national data up to 26/08/2014?
questions.note: Al's Q10. The physical testing data has not been supplied and is table data anyway. Must refuse.

questions.query: What does Allistair McCaw list as the E.Q. skills in coaching?
questions.note: Al's Q4. No McCaw file found by name. If the full index surfaces one, this expectation should flip.

questions.note: Al's Q7. Murphy, Duffield and Reid confirmed present in the extracted text.
